attrs.why: Bronchoalveolar lavage confirmed Pneumocystis organisms, together with perihilar ground-glass opacities, hypoxia (PO2 47 mmHg), elevated LDH (916 U/L) and oral thrush. Both expert analyses (pathologist and radiologist) independently endorse Pneumocystis pneumonia as the leading diagnosis and emphasize that negative bacterial/fungal cultures and negative HIV testing do not exclude it. Confidence raised from 0.95 to 0.96.

Fever, tachypnea and perihilar infiltrates could suggest bacterial pneumonia, but BAL cultures were negative and Pneumocystis organisms were identified; both experts consider bacterial pneumonia much less likely. Confidence lowered from 0.15 to 0.12.

Oral thrush and empirical fluconazole raised concern for fungal infection, but fungal cultures were negative with only oral Candida albicans isolated, and BAL confirmed Pneumocystis; experts regard invasive fungal pneumonia as unlikely. Confidence lowered from 0.1 to 0.08.

Ground-glass opacities and hypoxia could suggest interstitial lung disease, but BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis and the overall infectious picture make non-infectious ILD unlikely; both experts concur it is effectively ruled out. Confidence remains low at 0.05.

node-11.label: Patient was well-nourished (BMI 25.3) with no immunosuppressive risk factors, and HIV ELISA, Western blot and HIV-RNA PCR were all negative, indicating a non-immunocompromised host

attrs.why: BAL-confirmed Pneumocystis organisms in a well-nourished 32-year-old with no immunosuppressive risk factors and negative HIV testing indicate a non-HIV (immunocompetent host) form of Pneumocystis pneumonia. The pathologist explicitly notes that negative HIV testing does not exclude non-HIV PCP. Confidence 0.85, limited by the absence of CD4 count and lack of a defined immunodeficiency workup.

node-15.label: Idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL) as the underlying cause

attrs.why: Current frontier (node-14, 'Pneumocystis pneumonia in a non-HIV immunocompromised host with CD4 lymphocytopenia') identifies the immunodeficiency but not its cause; the belief states 'the main uncertainty is the underlying cause of the CD4 lymphocytopenia.' Node-3 and node-11 document no apparent immunosuppressive risk factors, no drugs, and negative HIV testing, and node-13 shows CD4 110 cells/µL with inverted CD4:CD8 0.35 — the classic profile of ICL, a diagnosis of exclusion and the most common recognized cause of non-HIV PCP.

node-16.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to hematologic malignancy (e.g., lymphoma)

attrs.why: Refines node-14 by attributing the low CD4 count (node-13) to an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder. Lymphoma can directly deplete CD4 T-cells and predispose to PCP in a non-HIV host. Elevated LDH (916 U/L, node-4) is a non-specific but supportive clue; however, there is no lymphadenopathy, B-symptoms, or abnormal routine blood work in node-2/node-4, so this remains an important but unconfirmed alternative.

node-17.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to drug or medication exposure

attrs.why: Refines node-14 by proposing exogenous/iatrogenic CD4 depletion. Certain immunosuppressants, chemotherapy, or other agents can reduce CD4 counts and permit PCP. Node-11 explicitly records 'no apparent immunosuppressive risk factors,' which argues against this, hence low confidence, but the history cannot be fully excluded and warrants verification.

node-18.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to an autoimmune or systemic disease

attrs.why: Refines node-14 by linking CD4 lymphocytopenia (node-13) to an underlying autoimmune/systemic disorder, a recognized secondary cause of low CD4 counts. Node-2 states the patient had 'no other accompanying symptoms,' and no autoantibody or systemic findings are recorded, so supporting evidence is absent and confidence is low.

node-19.label: CD4 lymphocytopenia secondary to chronic viral infection (e.g., HTLV-1)

attrs.why: Refines node-14 by considering a chronic retroviral/viral cause of CD4 depletion distinct from HIV, which was negative (node-6). HTLV-1 and similar agents can lower CD4 counts in non-HIV hosts, but no serology for these agents is present in the graph; node-6 only excludes HIV, so this remains an unverified, lower-probability hypothesis.
